Securitas Technology, part of Securitas, is a world-leading provider of integrated security solutions that protect, connect and optimise organisations across industries. With more than 13,000 colleagues in 40 countries, we deliver innovative technology platforms and services that help make the world a safer place.

In support of the broader business strategy, Securitas Technology Europe is undertaking a significant transformation programme to standardise business processes, modernise enterprise technology platforms, and establish a more integrated operating model across the region

Role Purpose

The Director of IT Transformation (Europe) is responsible for leading the delivery and ongoing development of Securitas Technology Europe's IT Transformation Roadmap. Working within a partially defined transformation agenda, the role will help shape, refine and execute a multi-year programme focused on modernising enterprise platforms, standardising business processes and enabling a more unified technology ecosystem across Europe.

Working closely with the European CIO, Business Transformation leadership team, European business leaders and regional IT teams, the Director of IT Transformation will ensure technology initiatives are aligned with business objectives and delivered effectively to support long-term operational efficiency, scalability and growth.

The role combines strategic programme leadership with hands-on transformation delivery, providing direction to cross-functional teams, managing transformation investments, and ensuring the successful adoption of new processes, systems and ways of working across multiple countries and business functions

Scope of Responsibility
Transformation Strategy & Roadmap

  • Lead the continued development and execution of the European IT Transformation Roadmap in alignment with the wider business transformation agenda.

  • Translate business priorities into a practical technology transformation strategy covering enterprise platforms, business applications, data capabilities and digital infrastructure.

  • Work with business and IT stakeholders to identify priorities, opportunities and transformation initiatives that support operational improvement and business growth.

  • Ensure technology investments support process standardisation, operational scalability and long-term organisational objectives.

Enterprise Programme Leadership

  • Lead large-scale, multi-country transformation programmes across Europe.

  • Oversee major modernisation initiatives involving ERP, CRM, enterprise applications, integrations and supporting data platforms.

  • Establish programme governance, delivery frameworks and reporting mechanisms that support effective delivery and transparent decision-making.

  • Manage programme plans, budgets, risks, resources, dependencies and delivery outcomes across multiple workstreams.

  • Ensure transformation initiatives are delivered on time, within scope and aligned to agreed business objectives.

Business & Technology Alignment

  • Partner with leaders across Sales, Operations, Finance, Supply Chain and other functional areas to ensure technology initiatives support business priorities.

  • Translate technology transformation objectives into practical business outcomes and process improvements.

  • Build strong relationships across business and technology teams to support alignment, engagement and successful programme execution.

  • Act as a trusted transformation partner to key stakeholders throughout programme planning and delivery

Technology Modernisation

  • Lead the modernisation of enterprise systems including ERP, CRM and supporting data platforms.

  • Drive initiatives that support adoption of modern cloud technologies, integrated business systems and scalable technology architecture.

  • Ensure transformation solutions align with organisational requirements for security, resilience, performance and sustainability.

  • Support the adoption of new technologies, tools and delivery approaches that enhance operational effectiveness and business value.

Leadership & Capability Development

  • Provide leadership, direction and support to IT transformation resources, programme teams, consultants and delivery partners.

  • Lead, coach and develop direct reports, creating a high-performing and collaborative team environment.

  • Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, continuous improvement and delivery excellence.

  • Ensure teams have the skills, capabilities and support needed to deliver complex transformation programmes successfully.

Vendor & Partner Collaboration

  • Develop and maintain effective relationships with strategic consulting partners and technology vendors.

  • Ensure external partners contribute effectively to programme delivery and remain aligned with transformation objectives.

  • Oversee supplier performance and support commercial governance activities relating to transformation programmes.

  • Collaborate with partners to leverage expertise, accelerate delivery and maximise programme outcomes.

Change Management & Adoption

  • Champion organisational change across business units and regions to support successful implementation of new systems and processes.

  • Work closely with change management and communications teams to embed transformation initiatives across the organisation.

  • Promote stakeholder engagement, user readiness and adoption throughout programme lifecycles.

  • Ensure technology transformation delivers measurable business benefits, productivity improvements and enhanced customer and colleague experiences

Performance, Governance & Investment Management

  • Establish and maintain governance frameworks that enable effective programme oversight and performance monitoring.

  • Define and track programme success measures, milestones and key performance indicators.

  • Own programme budgets and resource planning, ensuring effective allocation of investment and delivery resources.

  • Monitor programme performance and implement corrective actions where required to support successful outcomes.

  • Provide regular reporting and updates to senior stakeholders on programme progress, risks and opportunities.

Experience & Knowledge

  • Extensive experience leading large-scale IT, digital or business transformation programmes within complex organisations.

  • Proven track record delivering enterprise-wide ERP, CRM and business systems implementation or modernisation initiatives.

  • Experience with Oracle Fusion and Microsoft Dynamics 365 across ERP, Operations, CRM and HR modules

description:

Cherokee Nation Integrated Health (CNIH) is seeking a Health Communications Specialist to provide instructional design and training support services for the Global Border Health Team (GBHT) within CDC’s Division of Global Migration Health. GBHT supports partner countries in strengthening public health systems and workforce capacity to prevent, detect, and respond to communicable disease threats associated with population mobility and international travel. In this role, you will support the development, adaptation, delivery, and evaluation of training and learning products for partner countries, translating technical guidance into effective, learner-centered materials.

The successful candidate will possess strong instructional design, curriculum development, training, and communication skills, with the ability to adapt technical content for diverse audiences and country-specific contexts. This position offers an opportunity to support global public health capacity building through the development of training materials, eLearning products, job aids, toolkits, evaluation tools, and other learning resources designed to strengthen border health capabilities.

Compensation & Benefits: 80K/year

Pay commensurate with experience.

Full-time benefits include Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K, and other possible benefits as provided. Benefits are subject to change with or without notice.

Instructional Designer Responsibilities Include:

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

title: Industrial Design Intern
description:
Industrial Design Intern

Location: Los Angeles, CA (Onsite)
Compensation: $25-30/hr
Start date: Immediately
Duration: 3 months


About the Role

SprintRay is looking for an Industrial Design Intern who is excited to learn how physical products go from an idea to something customers use every day.

You'll work alongside industrial designers and mechanical engineers on SprintRay's resin 3D printing hardware for dental applications. This internship is focused on physical UX — how products look, feel, open, load, clean, and operate — and on learning how design decisions translate into manufacturable hardware.

This is a hands-on internship. You'll sketch, model, prototype, print, test, and iterate rather than spending all of your time behind a screen. We're looking for someone curious, resourceful, and excited to build things.


Key Responsibilities

  • Support industrial design development across SprintRay's hardware portfolio

  • Create sketches, CAD concepts, renderings, and presentation materials

  • Build physical prototypes using 3D printing, foam, and other rapid-prototyping methods

  • Help evaluate ergonomics, proportions, usability, and physical interactions

  • Work with industrial designers and mechanical engineers to iterate concepts

  • Assist with SolidWorks modeling and design development

  • Explore form, materials, finishes, and manufacturing approaches

  • Participate in design reviews and learn how concepts progress toward production

  • Help maintain design consistency across products and accessories

Required Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in Industrial Design, Product Design, or a related discipline

  • Portfolio demonstrating strong fundamentals in form, proportion, sketching, CAD, and physical product design

  • Comfortable building things by hand and rapidly prototyping ideas

  • Familiarity with SolidWorks; Rhino, KeyShot, or similar tools are a plus

  • Basic understanding of common manufacturing processes such as injection molding, CNC, or sheet metal

  • Strong curiosity and willingness to learn

  • Comfortable receiving feedback and iterating quickly

  • Interest in complex physical products, hardware, or consumer electronics

What You'll Learn

You'll get exposure to the full hardware-development process and work directly with designers and engineers developing real products. The goal is for you to leave the internship with stronger industrial design judgment, deeper manufacturing knowledge, and meaningful hands-on product-development experience.

Employment Type

Full-time internship, 3-6 months

About SprintRay

SprintRay is rewriting the rules of dentistry with technology that’s smart, fast, and designed to make life easier for dental professionals. Since 2014, we’ve been on a mission to deliver the most advanced 3D printing solutions in the industry—combining hardware, software, and materials into one seamless ecosystem.

But what really makes SprintRay different is our people. We’re a bold, global team of innovators, problem-solvers, and doers who thrive on pushing boundaries and challenging the status quo. Every product we create is driven by a simple goal: help dentists spend less time on repetitive tasks and more time changing patients’ lives.

Our culture is entrepreneurial, collaborative, and fueled by curiosity. We celebrate diverse perspectives and believe the best ideas can come from anywhere. Whether we’re building next-generation AI tools, designing new materials, or supporting our customers on the front lines, we’re united by the same passion—transforming digital dentistry and having fun while we do it.

At SprintRay, the future of dentistry is being printed today. Want to be part of it?

Makes appropriate adjustments/assignments to maximize timely patient care. Looks to staffing needs into the next matrix.

title: Switchboard Operator - Telecommunications - Full Time
description:
Be the voice that connects care. As Guthire's Switchboard Operator, you'll serve as the vital communication hub of our healthcare team, ensuring patients, families, physicians, and staff stay connected when it matters most. Your professionalism, compassion, and attention to detail will help support seamless patient care across the hospital.

About Guthrie Lourdes Hospital:
Join a 197-bed acute care hospital known for supporting its nurses and recognized nationally as a top place to work, including Modern Healthcare, Forbes, and Newsweek.

Schedule & Coverage:

Full Time, 3rd Shift, 9:30PM-6:00AM, and every other weekend

Position Summary:

Switchboard operators are responsible for courteous, efficient operation of Guthrie’s telecommunications system 24 hours a day. Operators field calls and inquiries, and direct internal and external calls to the proper destination. They are a vital link in the communication information network throughout the Guthrie system.

Education, License & Cert:

High school graduate or equivalent

Experience:

Prefer minimum of one year’s experience in the telecommunications field. Computer skills which include data entry, Windows XP, and Excel are required. Accurate and efficient keyboarding skills are necessary as well as fluency with the English language.

Essential Functions:

1. Activates approximately 25 codes for potentially life‐threatening situations.

a. Activates codes utilizing the overhead paging system and pagers and following a detailed checklist to ensure all essential personnel have been notified to respond to the emergency.

b. Responds immediately to correctly activate the codes as time is crucial to the patient’s well‐being. 2. Assists in answering an average of 3500‐4500 incoming calls on a daily basis.

3. Operates database for the Amcom system.

4. Creates and updates a daily on‐call sheet of over 90 providers and staff a. Distributes and updates on‐call list to the ED, Trauma Department, and Communications Center so that they are informed of vital information related to patient transfers from other facilities.

5. Provides after‐hours paging service for patient calls for several outlying Guthrie Entities.

6. Provides back‐up coverage for the patient information desk.

7. Monitors alarm panel.

a. Notifies proper department when the emergency alarm panel activates as a result of a malfunction. There are 43 alarms in this panel requiring exceptional judgment in responding.

8. Trains new operators. a. Assists in training new operators on all shifts to ensure they are competent to perform this job successfully.

9. Is required to problem‐solve and find solutions with little to no direction/supervision.

Other Duties:

1. Other duties as assigned.

The pay range for this position is $17.34-$23.96/hr. based on experience.

title: Performance Data Analyst
description:
About us

Procentia, part of the Brightwell Group, is an award-winning software and technology company specialising in the Pensions and Pension Risk Transfer/Bulk Purchase Annuities market. Established in 2002, the business is renowned for its web-based pensions administration and management system, IntelliPen.

Procentia’s products and solutions help pension schemes and administrators of all types and sizes manage exceptional volumes of data, meet the demand for self-serve technology, and provide meaningful, consumer-like experiences that users expect from modern online financial platforms while minimising the need for administrator intervention and involvement.

With offices in the UK and North America, Procentia supports some of the largest pension schemes, insurers and retirement plans across the private and public sectors, including BP, British Airways Pension Scheme, BTPS, Chicago Transit Authority, Legal & General Retirement America, Retirement System City of Detroit, Rolls-Royce, Royal London, and Universities Superannuation Scheme.

The job:

As part of our continued growth and transformation journey, we're looking for a Performance Data Analyst to join our Transformation and Organisational Effectiveness function. This role will establish the evidence needed to understand how effectively the business is operating and whether improvement activity is delivering the intended outcomes.

The role will bring together delivery and operational data, including information held in Azure DevOps, and turn it into clear, trusted insight through Power BI. Working across the organisation, you'll define measures, improve data quality, create repeatable reporting and help leaders and teams use performance information to make better decisions.

Here's what you'll be doing:

Building a clear view of performance - You'll work with stakeholders to define meaningful measures across productivity, throughput, quality, predictability, rework and benefits realisation.

• Extracting and preparing data - You'll query Azure DevOps and other agreed data sources, combine and transform data, and create reliable datasets for reporting and analysis.

• Developing Power BI reporting - You'll design, build and maintain accessible dashboards that show trends, exceptions, progress against targets and areas requiring attention.

• Turning data into insight - You'll interpret patterns, investigate variance and explain what the data means, helping teams move from reporting activity to taking action.

• Strengthening measurement discipline - You'll define data standards, calculation logic, ownership and reporting routines so measures are consistent, transparent and trusted.

• Supporting transformation and continuous improvement - You'll baseline current performance, track outcomes and provide evidence to prioritise and evaluate improvement activity across Catalyst and wider business initiatives.

Key skills and experience:

  • Strong ability to translate business objectives into meaningful KPIs, measures, data models, and actionable insights.

  • ·Proven experience analysing operational and delivery performance data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and areas for improvement.

  • Experience extracting, querying, validating, and analysing data from Azure DevOps, with knowledge of SQL and data transformation techniques.

  • Advanced Power BI skills, including Power Query, DAX, data modelling, dashboard development, and report maintenance.

  • Ability to develop clear, insightful reporting and dashboards that support decision-making and performance improvement.

  • Experience defining and measuring performance indicators, targets, and reporting frameworks.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to present evidence-based findings and practical recommendations.

  • Experience improving data quality, establishing consistent data definitions, and promoting good data management practices.

  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to gather requirements and explain complex information to different audiences.

  • Confidence presenting analysis and recommendations to senior stakeholders and leadership teams.

  • Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage priorities, maintain documentation, and deliver work independently.

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with PMO, transformation, product, technology, and operational teams to support performance improvement and data-driven decision-making.

Lets talk about what's in it for you...

· 25 days holiday (plus public holidays) increasing with length of service up to a maximum of 28 days, with carry over of up to 1 week

· Buying and Selling holiday (up to 1 week)

· Volunteer day

· 5% Employer contribution pension

· Life Assurance

· Private Medical Insurance

· Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)

· Health care cash plan

· Tusker – Electric Car Leasing scheme

Don’t meet every requirement?
We know that some candidates, particularly women, disabled people, LGBTQ+ individuals, neurodivergent people, and those from ethnic minority backgrounds, may hesitate to apply unless they meet every listed requirement. At Procentia, we’re committed to building a diverse, inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. If this role excites you but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every requirement, we encourage you to apply anyway. You could be a great fit for this role or another opportunity within our team.

title: Plant Environmental Safety & Health (ESH) Associate
description:
The ESH Associate supports the organization's commitment to maintaining a safe, healthy, and environmentally responsible workplace. This role partners with ESH leadership and plant management to implement, monitor, and continuously improve environmental, safety, and health programs in a 24/7 manufacturing environment, including flexibility to support off-shift needs as required. The role is an advisor to all employees from first line supervisors to leadership, with an intense focus on building the New Braunfels plant culture, partnerships, proactive problem solving, and excellent communication to deliver high quality customer service to all internal customers.

The expected annual salary range for this role is $67,680-75,200 a year depending on relevant experience. This position is also eligible for a variable incentive program.

In this role you will be working at our plant located at 440 Kohlenberg Rd, New Braunfels, TX 78130, on a daily basis.

Core Responsibilities

Legal and Other Requirements

  • Assist with monitoring environmental and safety programs to ensure compliance with federal and state legislation, OSHA occupational hazard and general industry safety requirements, and applicable federal, state, and local EPA regulations.
  • Support communication of compliance expectations and safety messaging across the site.

Hazard Prevention and Control

  • Conduct job safety and hazard analyses of manufacturing equipment.
  • Assist with key safety programs including Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), machine guarding, personal protective equipment (PPE), contractor safety, and workplace hazard reduction initiatives.
  • Participate in safety investigations, document root causes, and recommend corrective actions where hazards exist.
  • Identify hazardous behaviors and conditions and drive preventative and corrective actions to reduce risk.
  • Support safety programs through a regular presence on the production floor and in other facility areas as required.

Emergency Preparedness and Response

  • Coordinate Emergency Response Team (ERT) activities and annual employee evacuation drills, including maintaining evacuation maps and emergency procedures.
  • Support ERT recruiting and training efforts.
  • Maintain inventory, inspection records, and location documentation for emergency response equipment and supplies.

Safety Committee

  • Participate in or lead monthly safety committee meetings.
  • Maintain safety committee meeting minutes.
  • Communicate Environmental, Safety, and Health (ESH) initiatives across the site.
  • Track leading and lagging safety indicators.
  • Review safety metrics, action items, and improvement activities intended to reduce workplace hazards and strengthen overall safety performance.

Management Systems

  • Participate in site planning, development, and execution of strategic safety plans that support organizational objectives.
  • Manage safety-related PPE programs.
  • Partner with the ESH Leader and plant management team on safety and health initiatives and program management.
  • Assist with organizing and administering safety-related programs.
  • Implement tracking mechanisms and reporting tools to monitor ESH performance.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain standardized work instructions related to safety programs.

Training

  • Conduct ESH-related training as assigned, including new hire onboarding, annual compliance training, and task-specific safety training.
  • Support contractor management activities by ensuring completion of required induction training.
  • Monitor contractor work activities to ensure compliance with site safety requirements.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE ROLE

  • High School Diploma or GED required. Associate degree in Occupational Safety preferred. Bachelor's degree preferred.
  • 1 + years of experience in a manufacturing environment; safety experience preferred.
  • Working knowledge of OSHA occupational hazards and safety regulations for general industry.
  • Working knowledge of environmental compliance requirements, including federal, state, and local EPA regulations.
  • Experience supporting safety programs such as Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), machine guarding, personal protective equipment (PPE), contractor safety, emergency response, evacuation drills, and safety committee activities preferred.
  • Ability to plan and prioritize work, manage time effectively, and balance multiple responsibilities.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to proactively escalate issues when appropriate.
  • Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficiency in English required.
  • Ability to work effectively as a team member and interact with others in a professional and courteous manner.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Word, and Teams.
  • Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas now or in the future for this job posting.
  • Relocation assistance is not offered for this position.

Physical Requirements and Work Environment:

  • Must be able to wear company-provided safety-toed ESD shoes, smock, and other required PPE while working in designated production areas.
  • Must be able to sit or stand for extended periods of time, including shifts of 8 or more hours.
  • Must be able to reach, use hands and fingers, and operate computers and standard office equipment.
  • Must possess the manual dexterity necessary to operate computer keyboards, mice, and other technical instruments.
  • Must be able to spend time on the production floor and in other facility areas as required to support ESH initiatives and programs.

ADDITIONAL WAYS TO STAND OUT

  • Master Degree
  • Professional Certifications: CSP, CIH, CHMM, CEM, OSHA 30/50, ISO internal auditor certifications.
  • Experience in greenfield manufacturing, plant startup, or plant expansion environments.
  • Experience leading ESH teams or cross‑functional groups.
  • Experience with industrial hygiene monitoring, fire protection systems, or security operations.
  • Experience with EHS software (SafePulse).
  • Ability to analyze ESH data and prepare dashboards/reports.
  • Familiarity with digital tools for risk assessment, audits, or training.

THE PERKS

  • Employees 401k Match
  • Diverse & Inclusive Work Environment with 20+ Employee Resource groups.

location: New York, New York, United States of America
description:
The ABC News New York Bureau serves as the New York hub, leading breaking news coverage, enterprise reporting, and editorial coordination across the Eastern United States. The bureau plays a critical role in identifying, developing, and executing coverage of major national stories while partnering closely with network broadcasts, digital platforms, News Services, Audio, and Owned Television Stations.

The bureau oversees day-to-day newsgathering operations, manages field coverage, and deploys resources to support ABC News' editorial priorities—working in close partnership with the broader Global Newsgathering organization.

Under the direction of the Manager on Duty, Segment Producer, or Assignment Editor, the Media Coordinator supports daily newsgathering and content distribution operations across broadcast, digital, and affiliate platforms.

Responsibilities:

  • Assist with media ingest operations, including digital file conversion, importing content, and transferring media from third-party sources.
  • Prepare and distribute video cuts for affiliates, clients, OTV stations, and digital platforms.
  • Draft and format voiceover (VO) scripts for affiliate and client use with ABC News content.
  • Maintain and organize media assets within Pyramid and Extreme Reach systems.

Required Skills:

title: APRN – Community Mental Health
description:
Salary: $140,000 + DOQ/DOE

Location: Salt Lake City, UT

Schedule: Full-Time

Setting: Field-Based (ACT Team)


Benefits

  • Low-cost medical, dental, and vision coverage. Health savings account. 403b retirement plan with employer match (50% match up to 3%).
  • Employee Assistance Program for all employees.
  • 33 paid days off: 11 observed paid holidays, 12 sick days, and 10 vacation days to start. Vacation increases to 12 days after 1 year, 15 days after 2 years, and more at 5 and 9 years of service.
    • Sick and vacation time accrue hourly per pay period.
  • $50,000 in employer-paid life insurance; additional coverage available.
  • Employer contribution to your Health Savings Account (paid quarterly).
  • Employee Referral Program including cash bonuses and paid time off.
  • Public Service Loan Forgiveness eligible.


About

Volunteers of America, Utah is an affiliate of a national, nonprofit, faith-based organization that has served communities across the United States for more than 125 years. Volunteers of America, Utah’s mission is to provide community-supported paths for those who are vulnerable to improve their lives and increase their self-reliance. Our programs serve people experiencing challenges related to mental health, substance use, and homelessness. We encourage all who are passionate about making a difference, including individuals with lived experience, to apply.


Make a Real Impact in Your Community


Join Volunteers of America, Utah, as a Psychiatric APRN on our Assertive Community Treatment (ACT) team—a nationally recognized, evidence-based model that delivers care where it's needed most: in the homes and neighborhoods of people with serious mental illness (SMI). This is not your typical clinic job. If you're passionate about high-impact, human-centered care, we want to hear from you.


Volunteers of America, Utah's ACT Team members directly provide services that are individually tailored with each client and address their specific preferences and goals. The approach with each client emphasizes the relationship building and active involvement in assisting clients to make improvements in functioning, to better manage symptoms, to achieve individual goals and to maintain optimism.


What You'll Do

  • Provide psychiatric assessments, medication management, and clinical oversight to individuals living with SMI
  • Deliver care in community and home-based settings alongside a multidisciplinary ACT team
  • Build long-term therapeutic relationships and help clients stay out of the hospital
  • Participate in crisis intervention, team planning, and recovery-focused care coordination
  • Enjoy autonomy, but never isolation—work with a supportive psychiatrist and clinical team

What We’re Looking For

  • Licensed APRN in Utah (or ability to obtain) with prescriptive authority
  • At least 1 year of psychiatric experience—inpatient or community mental health preferred
  • Comfortable working in field settings and with clients facing complex behavioral health challenges
  • Clear communication, sound clinical judgment, and strong documentation skills
  • Must be 21+, pass a drug screen and background check, and have a valid driver’s license


Essential Duties:

  • Collaborate with the team leader, psychiatrist, and entire Assertive Community Treatment team in sharing overall clinical responsibility for monitoring consumer treatment and take a lead role in coordinating and providing the team’s medication administration services
  • Conduct psychiatric assessments including psychiatric history (e.g., onset, course and effect of illness, past treatment and responses, and risk behaviors), mental status, and diagnoses; use of drugs or alcohol; education and employment; social development and functioning; activities of daily living; family structure and relationships; and physical health, making appropriate referrals to community physicians as necessary
  • Prescribe psychotropic medications; conduct regular assessments of therapeutic responses and side effects; and educate clients and non-medical staff on medications and their side effects
  • Be actively involved in both acute and long-term psychiatric inpatient treatment of clients
  • Provide on-call crisis intervention and participate in on-call rotation
  • Works with consumers and staff to develop and implement person-centered individual treatment plans that address psychiatric issues and align with clients' goals and preferences
  • Participate in daily staff organizational meetings and treatment planning review meetings
  • Complete documentation and meet minimum service time based on ACT requirements
  • Performing work on site is required to provide direct client care. This includes care in the community such as in patients’ homes, resource centers, streets, etc.

title: Salesforce Solutions Architect
description:
Salesforce Solutions Architect

(Platform Enablement, Solution Design, and Best-Practice Implementation)

Engagement Type: Full-time / Permanent
Location: Satellite Office Location (preferred alignment with U.S. business hours)
Working Hours: Requires overlap with U.S. Central Time business hours

Reports To: Salesforce Program Manager

Role Overview

We are seeking a highly experienced Salesforce Solutions Architect to serve as a strategic and hands-on partner in maximizing the effectiveness of our Salesforce platform. This role is responsible for evaluating the current Salesforce implementation, identifying opportunities to improve how the platform supports sales and service operations, and designing and building scalable, best-practice solutions within Salesforce.

The architect will work closely with Salesforce Delivery Lead, Administrators, and business stakeholders. This is a delivery-focused architect role and is expected to assess the day-today use of Salesforce, identify gaps or inefficiencies in platform utilization, translate those insights into well-architected design solutions. Will require building / refactoring solutions while also establishing the standards, integration patterns, and governance guardrails that keep the platform healthy as it grows.

This role balances platform enablement and business partnership with strong architectural governance and implementation discipline, ensuring improvements enhance business outcomes without introducing unnecessary complexity or technical debt.

Key Responsibilities

Platform Enablement & Business Partnership

  • Partner closely with Salesforce Administrators and business stakeholders to understand how Salesforce currently supports sales and service workflows.

  • Evaluate platform usage, user adoption, and workflow execution to identify opportunities for improvement in efficiency, usability, and effectiveness.

  • Recommend platform enhancements that enable sales and service teams while remaining aligned with Salesforce with best practices and architectural standards.

  • Act as a trusted advisor by connecting platform design decisions to operational outcomes (revenue, cost, productivity, risk, customer experience), ensuring Salesforce capabilities are used intentionally and appropriately.

Salesforce Org Assessment & Architecture

  • Conduct a comprehensive assessment of the existing Salesforce org, including:

    • Data model, data quality, standard and custom objects

    • Automation (Flows, legacy Process Builder and workflows)

    • Security model, profiles, permission sets, and sharing

    • Integrations, APIs, and data flows

    • Technical debt, scalability risks, and performance concerns

  • Identify architectural anti-patterns and areas where the platform has been over- or under-customized.

  • Document findings and present clear, actionable recommendations.

Roadmap, Standards & Governance

  • Develop a prioritized roadmap that balances near-term business enablement with long-term platform health.

  • Define and document Salesforce standards and guardrails, including:

    • Naming conventions and configuration guidelines

    • Automation and integration patterns

    • Data quality and lifecycle management practices

    • Sandbox strategy, deployment, and release / change management

  • Establish governance practices that enable innovation while preventing future technical debt.

Implementation & Delivery

  • Lead and execute the implementation of new Salesforce modules and capabilities (e.g., Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, custom solutions).

  • Refactor or redesign existing configurations and automation to improve scalability, maintainability, and alignment with standards.

  • Design and implement integrations with external systems using APIs or middleware where appropriate.

  • Ensure changes are properly tested, deployed, and documented.

Collaboration & Knowledge Transfer

  • Produce clear documentation to support long-term ownership, maintainability, and operational continuity.

  • Collaborate with internal teams and external partners to ensure consistent architectural alignment.

  • Mentor and support Salesforce Administrators by reinforcing best practices, architectural principles, and enable upskilling internal resources.

Required Skill & Qualifications

  • 8–15+ years of Salesforce of deep expertise and hands on in the following areas:

    • Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, CPQ, and related Salesforce products

    • Apex, Lightning Web Components (LWC), declarative automation (Flows), and Salesforce security

    • Integration technologies (REST/SOAP APIs, middleware, external systems)

    • Enterprise data modeling, migration, and governance

    • CI/CD, DevOps, Salesforce DX, and structured release management practices

    • Salesforce configuration and customization

    • Data modeling and security architecture

    • Significant responsibility for solution design and architecture

  • Demonstrated experience evaluating existing Salesforce implementations and driving platform improvements

  • Proven ability to balance business needs with technical discipline and platform standards.

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical decisions in business terms.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Salesforce certifications such as:

    • Salesforce Certified Application Architect

    • Salesforce Certified System Architect

    • Salesforce Certified Technical Architect (CTA) or progress toward CTA

  • Experience working in environments with complex sales, service operations, and / or multi-org Salesforce implementations.

  • Prior consulting or advisory experience performing org assessments and roadmap development.

  • Ticket management systems Fresh Service, Service Now

  • Agile Methodologies / Jira

What Success Looks Like

  • Salesforce is better aligned to how sales and service teams operate, with improved usability and adoption.

  • Clear, documented standards and architectural guardrails are in place and being followed.

  • New capabilities are implemented cleanly, with minimal rework and reduced technical debt.

  • Salesforce Administrators are supported and enabled with clearer guidance and structure.

  • The platform is positioned to scale while continuing to support evolving business needs.

title: Director of Product, Media Plan Management
description:
About Guideline

Guideline is a global provider of ad intelligence and media plan management technology, powering the strategy, planning, and management of advertising buying and selling for the world’s leading enterprises. Our solutions deliver the industry’s most comprehensive and timely insights, enabling publishers, agencies, brands, investors, and consulting firms to optimize media performance and drive superior business outcomes.

Guideline’s proprietary spend and pricing data represents approximately $200 billion in annual media investment across 65 countries, providing the most complete and transparent view of the global advertising marketplace available today. In 2026 we are accelerating our investment in analytics and AI-powered solutions for the advertising and capital markets industries.


About the Role

Guideline is the leading provider of Media Plan Management solutions through Mediatools and Lumina. Today, the world's largest agencies manage billions of dollars in ad spend across fragmented systems, resulting in inconsistent taxonomies, manual reporting processes, and limited real-time visibility into media plans.


Reporting directly to the SVP of Media Plan Management, this role is responsible for defining and delivering the product capabilities that solve these challenges across both platforms. You will own the end-to-end media planning experience—including plans, flights, approvals, briefs, budgets, and related workflows ensuring a consistent, scalable experience in both Mediatools and Lumina.


Key Responsibilities

  • Define how each core use case should work, and decide what has to be identical across our Media Plan Management solutions.
  • Prioritize what ships, and when, for the core workflow areas: media plans, flights, approvals, briefs, and budgets, across platforms.
  • Own the commercial outcome of these use cases: what's driving expansion, what's putting retention at risk, and where a new capability or pricing change would move the needle, on either platform.
  • Use Guideline's AI and MCP Server infrastructure as the shared lever for both platforms: features that beat feature parity, not just match it.
  • Bring client and market reality into the room with leadership. Every call here should trace back to something a client actually said or did, not a hunch.
  • Work directly with agencies and brands to build the workflows and solutions they actually need, not just what's already scoped.
  • Build and ship the way the rest of the team does: AI, API, and MCP-first, with agents and skills as a normal part of the workflow, not a special project.

Required Skills & Experience

  • 10–14 years in product management with real depth in media planning, buying, or agency workflow tools.
  • Has owned a workflow or capability that had to work the same way across more than one product or platform, not just one owned end to end.
  • Has owned a product with direct commercial accountability. Understands how product decisions translate into expansion, retention, and revenue, not just usage.
  • Understands how brand and agency users pull in different directions on the same platform, and has built for both sides.
  • Comfortable owning a single set of use cases that has to work across two different platforms, each with its own architecture and constraints.
  • Operates at Director scope as an IC. Earns influence through quality of thinking and earned credibility, not authority.
  • Builds and deploys AI agents and skills, and works comfortably with APIs and MCP as core design primitives, as part of everyday work; a baseline at this level, not a differentiator.

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Direct experience with media planning platforms (Camphouse, Mediaocean/Prisma, MINT, or similar) as a builder, buyer, or user.
  • Familiarity with agentic AI in planning workflows: quality scoring, suggestions, benchmarking, or similar AI-assisted features.
  • Experience expanding usage within agency or brand accounts. Understands the motion that turns product adoption into revenue.
  • Background solving this with a shared design system or component library, not just tribal knowledge passed between teams.
  • Familiarity with multi-market governance or global agency/brand account structures.

Benefits: Guideline offers full- time employees a comprehensive benefits package based on location. Some benefits may include, but are not limited to: • Medical, Dental, Vision, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Account • STD, Life, LTD and AD&D • 401(k) with a company match program • Unlimited Paid Time Off (PTO) • Paid Parental Leave • Commuter Benefits • Employee Recognition Program • Referral Bonus Program


Equal Opportunity Employer: Guideline is an equal opportunity employer, committed to our diversity and inclusiveness. We will consider all qualified applicants ithout regard to race, color, nationality, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, disability, or age. We strongly encourage women, people of color, members of the LGBTQIA community, people with disabilities, and veterans to apply.

title: Director, Operations & Strategy
description:

We are a purpose-driven, dynamic and sustainable pension plan. Don’t just work anywhere — come build tomorrow together with us.

Know someone at OMERS or Oxford Properties? Great! If you're referred, have them submit your name through Workday first. Then, watch for a unique link in your email to apply.

Director, Operations & Strategy

OMERS Private Equity is looking for a Director to join our Operations & Strategy team in New York.

This role will work closely with OMERS Private Equity (OPE)’s investment team and portfolio companies to drive operational and strategic improvements in specific portfolio companies as well as enhance our capability to do so repeatably and at scale across the portfolio.

The successful candidate will be a business athlete with significant experience in identifying key value creation opportunities, structuring, and executing analysis, and leading implementation and change in organizations. This role requires in-office presence as well as travel to portfolio companies and Toronto as needed.

In this position, you will be responsible for:

  • Leading high-value value engagements across 1-4 portfolio companies at any given time. Engagements will be targeted in nature, operating in a hands-on advisory capacity for a discreet time period, and, if needed, take on interim roles in our portfolio companies.

  • Contributing an operational perspective to Diligence through identifying and quantifying value creation opportunities and assessing the management team’s ability to capture those opportunities,

  • Ensuring that a robust value creation plan is in place in all portfolio investments by providing direction on key areas of focus, such as idea generation, alignment facilitation, plan execution, support and resource planning, and relationship management with management teams and other stakeholders.

  • Engaging with senior management as a trusted thought partner and problem solver to ensure they deliver the value creation plan.

  • Frequently and directly advancing the 1-2 most important value creation initiatives in your portfolio companies.

  • Partnering with other members of the Operations and Strategy team to play an active role in advancing the portfolio and asset management model for OPE. Serving as a change agent who is always looking for the next level of performance and leading initiatives to ensure best practices are employed across the portfolio.

  • Mentoring and developing junior colleagues.

  • Building and maintaining effective relationships internally at OMERS and OPE, and externally across boards, executive teams and third-party advisors.

Required Capabilities:

  • 10+ years of professional experience including leadership roles, management consulting, and private equity, as well as an understanding of multiple industries reflective of our portfolio

  • Proven experience in strategic planning and strategy development

  • Experience managing multiple projects and working with a diverse range of internal and external stakeholders

  • Track record of value creation through executing revenue and operational improvement initiatives

  • Transaction and due diligence experience

  • Strategic and results oriented mindset, takes a proactive, hands-on approach

Preferred Capabilities:

  • An ability to constructively challenge the status quo

  • Strong commercial acumen, understands multiple business drivers

  • Strong influencing and collaboration skills, and the ability to effect change through advice, counsel and action

About OMERS Private Equity

OMERS Private Equity (OPE) is the private equity investment arm of OMERS, one of Canada’s largest defined benefit pension plans, with approximately C$145 billion in net assets. Established in 1962, OMERS administers pensions for over 665,000 members from over 1,000 employers, including municipalities, school boards, emergency services, and local agencies across Ontario. With a global presence and offices in Toronto (headquarters), New York, London, Sydney, and Singapore, OMERS manages a diversified portfolio spanning public markets, private equity, infrastructure, and real estate, with the majority of capital invested directly.


OPE is a thesis-driven private equity sponsor with a flexible mandate to pursue control buyouts and opportunistic structured or minority investments, with approximately C$25B in AUM. The team typically targets initial equity investments of $200–500 million in companies generating $25–50 million of EBITDA, focusing on high-quality businesses in large, scalable markets with recurring or re-occurring revenue models. OPE’s sector focus includes business and tech-enabled services, industrials, and healthcare.

OPE strives to:

  • Partner with Management collaboratively and respectfully

  • Focus on building long-term, sustainable growth

  • Bring selective external expertise where and when needed

  • Support ongoing growth via the OMERS capital base

  • Reinvest to accelerate sustainable success versus “stripping out” capital for returns based purely on financial engineering

At its core, OPE is relentlessly focused on generating consistently compelling risk-adjusted returns for its 665,000 plan members.

The annualized base salary ranges for the primary location and any additional locations are listed below. The base salary that is ultimately offered to the successful candidate will consider a wide array of factors including but not limited to the individual’s skill set.

The expected salary range for this position is $230,000.00 - $330,000.00 per year.

You may also be eligible to receive an annual Incentive Award pursuant to our Short-term Incentive plan and our Long-Term Incentive plan (if applicable), and to participate in our group benefits and retirement plans – details on these elements of compensation are included within OMERS & Oxford offer letters.

As one of Canada’s largest defined benefit pension plans, our people-first culture is at its best when our workforce reflects the communities where we live and work — and the members we proudly serve.

From hire to retire, we are an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment and selection process that extends all the way through your employee experience. This sense of belonging and connection is cultivated up, down and across our global organization thanks to our vast network of Employee Resource Groups with executive leader sponsorship, our Purpose@Work committee and employee recognition programs.

title: Operations & Supply Chain Specialist - South Africa based
description:
WELCOME!



We are looking for a highly organised, analytical, and commercially minded Operations & Supply Chain Specialist to join our growing distribution business.

The ideal candidate is experienced in coordinating supply chain operations, managing suppliers, tracking inventory, and keeping orders moving across international markets. This role requires strong attention to detail, excellent communication, and the ability to take ownership in a fast-moving, remote environment. The successful candidate will work closely with US leadership, manufacturing partners, overseas suppliers, third-party logistics providers, and retail customers.

Who We Are

We are a US-based national distribution business supplying compliant hemp products and vaporisation hardware to independent retailers across the United States — smoke shops, specialty CBD stores, and convenience channels — with licensed partners internationally. The company runs a lean, modern operation: just-in-time supply chain, US finished-goods manufacturing partners, third-party logistics (3PL) fulfilment, overseas component suppliers, and a small senior team that uses AI aggressively to work like a team many times its size. This role is a full-time, remote position based in South Africa, employed through an employer-of-record arrangement, working closely with the US leadership team.

Overview

You will run the engine room of a national distribution supply chain. The flow: packaging and hardware come from overseas suppliers to US-based finished-goods manufacturing partners — hemp manufacturers who formulate and fill the materials into vape devices, gummies, and pre-roll products — and finished goods move out through US 3PL warehouses to retailers nationwide, with packaging and hardware also shipping to licensed partners internationally. The company operates just-in-time, so precision and early warning matter more than anything. This is a data-heavy, AI-forward, automation-forward role: we want someone who builds toward accurate forecasts and an efficient supply chain model, and whose reflex is that anything done manually, repetitively, or daily should be automated.

Key Responsibilities

  • Create and manage purchase orders with overseas suppliers (packaging and hardware, primarily China), tracking lead times and follow-ups.

  • Coordinate daily with US-based finished-goods manufacturing partners: packaging and hardware arriving on time, production schedules on track, finished goods flowing to the 3PLs.

  • Drive the sales & operations planning (S&OP) process: demand forecasting, supply planning, and continuous improvement of forecast accuracy.

  • Coordinate daily with US-based 3PL warehouses: inbound receipts, fulfillment quality, exceptions —everything coming in and going out, properly.

  • Coordinate international shipments of packaging and hardware to licensed partners in Europe and other countries.

  • Track inventory positions and reorder points; flag stock-out risk early, every time.

  • Run the order desk: order processing and fulfillment support for a national retailer network.

  • Automate relentlessly: build AI-driven automations for reporting, tracking, and routine coordination — anything manual, repetitive, or daily is a target.

  • Build and maintain the data layer: forecast models, supply chain KPIs, and efficiency reporting

Requirements

  • Based in South Africa.

  • 3+ years in supply chain, purchasing, or operations for a distribution, CPG, or e-commerce business.

  • Demonstrated AI fluency — you use AI tools every day, you've automated real workflows in a previous role, and you can walk us through examples.

  • Real forecasting and S&OP experience — comfortable building the model, not just running it.

  • Hands-on coordination experience with 3PLs and/or contract manufacturers.

  • Strong analytical toolkit: advanced spreadsheets required, ERP experience strongly preferred.

  • Extreme attention to detail and follow-through.

  • Fluent business English; able to work a split schedule covering China and US time windows

Bonus Points

  • Direct experience with Chinese manufacturers and freight forwarders.

  • Contract manufacturing / co-packer coordination in CPG.

  • Just-in-time or lean inventory management; landed-cost analysis and import/export documentation.

  • Experience supporting a fast-scaling retail distribution network

Details

  • Fully Remote | Based in South Africa

  • Salary: $2500 monthly, based on experience

  • Schedule: Split coverage by design (overlap with both China-based suppliers and US East Coast business hours)

Benefits of Joining Our Team

  • Opportunities for professional growth and career development.

  • Collaborative and supportive working environment.

  • Ongoing training and professional development.

  • Opportunity to help build and improve a modern international supply chain.

  • Exposure to suppliers, manufacturers, logistics providers, fulfilment operations, and retail distribution.

  • Meaningful responsibility and the opportunity to make a direct impact in a lean, growing business.

title: Teamlead Sourcing CZ
description:
Key position in a rapidly growing international integrated supply environment

Organization

MAG45, headquartered in Eindhoven, the Netherlands, is one of Europe’s leading industrial integrators. As an industrial integrator, we manage our customers’ supply chains, including procurement, for MRO (Maintenance, Repair & Operations) and BOM (Bill of Materials) products.

As one of the pioneers in integrated supply, we have built a successful international track record with multinational companies in the medical, high-tech, pharmaceutical, FMCG and electronics industries. Founded in 1948, we are growing rapidly and are now active in 16 countries worldwide. Since 2016, we have been a wholly owned subsidiary of the Danish listed Solar Group, and we are continuing to pursue profitable growth through our new strategy.

MAG45 has been present in the Czech Republic since 2007. Today, our team of around 25 employees in Brno is focused on further strengthening and developing our local commercial, operational and procurement activities. To further professionalize our local supply chain, we are looking for a Teamlead Sourcing.

Position

As Teamlead Sourcing, you play a key role in strengthening our local supply chain in the Czech Republic. You ensure that we work with the right suppliers and know how to balance and connect quality, delivery reliability, logistics, technology and financial performance. Through your approach, you will not only improve the supply chain, but also directly contribute to greater delivery reliability, healthy margins and revenue growth.

You take a broad, strategic perspective and actively collaborate with internal and external stakeholders. In line with the MAG45 category strategy, you continuously identify opportunities for optimization and turn them into tangible results. You negotiate with suppliers, build strong and sustainable relationships, and ensure that agreements are effectively implemented.

In addition, you will be involved in project-based supply chain challenges for our current and prospective customers from a Procurement perspective. You are responsible for all procurement-related activities involved in assessing and implementing supply chain solutions. Your key objective is to achieve the best Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) for our customers.

You will also ensure that product and supplier data in our ERP system is complete, accurate and up to date. In doing so, you provide an important foundation for a reliable and efficient operation.

As Teamlead Sourcing, you combine strategic insight with operational drive. You provide functional leadership to the procurement employees in Brno and work closely with your Procurement colleagues in Eindhoven, the Netherlands. You report hierarchically to the Country Manager Czech Republic and functionally to the Senior Sourcing Specialist in Eindhoven.

Requirements

We are looking for a strong and structured professional who is able to independently manage and further develop a local supply chain. Someone who enjoys building, improving and continuously optimizing. You bring:

  • A completed higher professional education degree (HBO level or equivalent), preferably in Supply Chain, Engineering or a related field

  • At least five years of relevant experience in an international trading or manufacturing environment

  • Excellent command of Czech and English, both written and spoken

  • Experience with contract management and tender processes

  • An affinity with technical products

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to convincingly engage with stakeholders at different organizational levels

What we offer

You will join a financially healthy organization with a distinctive value proposition. Our strong growth brings a dynamic and fast-paced environment, while also offering you the opportunity to take responsibility and help shape the further professionalization of the organization.

This is a role where you can make a real impact.

You will become part of a relatively small local team operating in an international environment, with international customers and colleagues around the world. MAG45 is characterized by short communication lines and offers plenty of room for initiative, entrepreneurship, personal development and career growth.

Your onboarding program will be tailored to your needs and will include, among other things, training in the Netherlands. Excellent primary and secondary employment conditions complete the package.

We initially offer a one-year employment contract, which, subject to mutual agreement, will be converted into a permanent contract.

Apply

Interested? Apply today with your English-language CV via the application button. As part of the application process, candidates will be asked to complete an online assessment and provide two written references.

title: Residential Counselor FT (68964)
company: Volunteers of America Chesapeake and Carolinas
description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Volunteers of America Chesapeake & Carolinas empowers self-reliance and inspires hope. As a church without walls, we do this through personalized housing, ministry, health, and human services that benefit vulnerable individuals, their families and the community. Founded in 1896 in Baltimore, MD by social reformers, Ballington and Maud Booth, we were one of the first of over 30 affiliates of Volunteers of America – one of the nation’s largest and most comprehensive human services organizations.

Our founders envisioned a movement dedicated to reaching and uplifting the American people. On behalf of the organization, the Booths pledged “to go wherever we are needed, and do whatever comes to hand”. Their declaration continues to guide Volunteers of America's impact on “Helping America’s most vulnerable”.

Through a dedicated and committed team of more than 850 employees and thousands of volunteers, we provide critical care, support services and hope to thousands of people each year throughout Virginia, Maryland, the District of Columbia and the Carolinas. We firmly believe our employees drive the success of the organization. Through our diversity, equity and inclusion efforts, we endeavor to attract, engage and retain qualified, diverse, compassionate individuals to join our journey and experience a work environment that offers challenging, stimulating and financially rewarding opportunities.

JOB SUMMARY

Reporting to the group homes’ Residential Coordinator, but under the clinical supervision of the Rehabilitation Director, the Residential Counselor is responsible for the provision of direct services which promote the ability of clients to participate in appropriate community activities and which contribute to the development and utilization of skills necessary for independent living. Additionally, the Residential Counselor will participate in the assessment of the client's rehabilitation needs and, in the development, implementation and monitoring of the client's individual rehabilitation plan. The Residential Counselor is also responsible for providing crisis services, including intensive support and assistance, and may be required to provide follow-along services to suspended or discharged clients. The Residential Counselor is responsible for driving and/or transporting clients.

The Residential Counselor is also responsible for ensuring that clients develop and utilize skills that contribute to the maintenance of a safe residential environment as well as documenting service delivery. The Residential Counselor may be privileged to provide basic health teaching in the areas of nutrition, exercise, dental care, substance abuse prevention, and prevention of injury and illness at home and in the community as well as training in communicable disease prevention.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Participates in the assessment of clients' rehabilitative service needs and, in the development, implementation and monitoring of the individual's rehabilitation plan
  • Coordinates activities and delivers rehabilitation and support services which address individual client goals and objectives contained within the client's rehabilitation plan which are directed toward the development or restoration of independent living skills.
  • Such activities may include the development or restoration of self-care skills including personal hygiene, grooming, menu planning and preparation, socialization skills, independent living skills, including the maintenance of the individual's living environment, community awareness, mobility skills and/or money management.
  • The Residential Counselor may be privileged to provide health teaching and prevention of communicable diseases.
  • Provides basic supervision in home-like environments for individuals with varying levels of mental illness.
  • Coordinates activities which promote community integration.

title: Applied Scientist / AI Research Engineer
description:
About Zinkworks

Zinkworks partners with leading Telecommunications and Financial Services organizations to modernize legacy systems, migrate mission-critical platforms to the cloud, and engineer AI-driven automation. From OSS transformation to rApp development and network intelligence, our teams simplify complexity and turn it into competitive advantage. Based in Ireland and operating across the EU, UK, and US, Zinkworks combines deep domain expertise with delivery excellence to help clients modernize faster and operate smarter.

The Role

Zinkworks is building a small product discovery team developing AI and machine learning capabilities for next-generation telecom networks, taking new product ideas from concept through to working prototypes.

We are looking for a senior applied scientist to lead the design of the machine learning methods behind these products. Working on complex problems in network data, you will determine the most appropriate modelling approaches, weigh the trade-offs, and build and validate the prototypes that prove them out. It is a hands-on role that combines research judgement with strong engineering practice, suited to someone equally comfortable selecting a method and implementing it.

What You'll Do

  • Own method and model selection for the team's hardest ML problems, and defend the trade-offs with reasoning and evidence.

  • Turn ambiguous, real-world problems into sound ML approaches, and build the prototypes that test them.

  • Validate and challenge modelling decisions across the team; keep the bar high so "it should work" is always backed by evidence.

  • Adapt state-of-the-art techniques from the literature to the realities of messy operational data.

  • Work closely with domain experts to frame problems correctly, and with engineering colleagues to make prototypes production-ready.

What You Bring

  • Genuine depth in ML modelling: you can design, train, and critically evaluate models, not just call an API. Strong across several of: graph learning, spatio-temporal / time-series modelling, reinforcement learning, and causal inference.

  • A track record of taking a novel or ill-defined problem all the way to a working, validated model.

  • Strong Python and hands-on engineering; comfortable prototyping on cloud ML platforms (ideally GCP / Vertex AI).

  • The ability to justify method choices to technical and non-technical people, and to change your mind when the evidence says so.

  • Comfort in a fast-moving discovery environment with minimal support scaffolding, seeing problems through from question to working solution.

Nice to Have

  • Telecoms, network-operations, or other complex real-time systems exposure.

  • Experience applying ML to large-scale operational or sensor/time-series data.

  • PhD or equivalent research depth in ML, paired with a record of shipping rather than pure academia.

  • Familiarity with LLM/agentic patterns as one tool among many, not the whole toolbox.

  • Publications or open-source work that demonstrate applied rigour.

Inclusion & Diversity at Zinkworks

At Zinkworks, we are deeply committed to fostering a culture of diversity, inclusion, and belonging. We believe that our strength lies in the unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences of our team members. By embracing an inclusive environment, we empower innovation and collaboration across all levels of our organisation. Based in Ireland, we are proud to support and engage with our local communities through meaningful initiatives that promote equity and opportunity. Our commitment extends beyond the workplace, as we actively contribute to creating a more inclusive and connected society for all.

Our teams work with technologies like Databricks, Snowflake, dbt, and the broader Microsoft ecosystem to turn messy, real-world data into trustworthy, actionable insight.

Position overview:

Blue Orange Digital is seeking a Senior Data Governance Lead for a part-time advisory role spanning Weeks 2-18 of a 26-week enterprise data warehouse implementation for a global commodities trading and supply chain company. You will design and implement the data governance framework for a Microsoft Fabric platform built over fragmented legacy data - multiple regional ERPs, CTRM instances (including Irely), and a concurrent SAP S/4HANA finance transformation - spanning trading, risk, finance, and logistics data domains. This is a greenfield governance engagement with high influence and real production impact on a modern Fabric architecture.

Responsibilities:

  • Establish end-to-end data lineage tracking from source systems (ERP, CTRM, SAP) through transformation layers to final reporting data products

  • Develop and apply data quality rules and validation frameworks across ingestion and transformation layers, integrated with Fabric pipeline execution

  • Define naming conventions, data classification standards, and workspace-level access control policies in alignment with Fabric governance capabilities

  • Collaborate with SAP S/4HANA and CTRM integration workstreams to document source-system metadata and lineage for all key data domains

  • Develop and lead master data management strategy for key shared entities across trading, finance, and logistics domains

  • Produce governance documentation, data stewardship process guides, and training materials for client data owners and analysts

Requirements:

  • 7+ years in data governance, data management, or data architecture with production governance framework implementations

  • Experience with Microsoft Azure or Fabric governance capabilities - Microsoft Purview a strong advantage for OneLake/Fabric cataloging and lineage

  • Strong background in data lineage, metadata management, and data quality frameworks at enterprise scale

  • Familiarity with financial or commodity trading data domains and the governance complexity of multi-source, cross-domain environments

  • Experience defining stewardship processes and working with business owners to operationalize governance policies

  • Bachelor's degree in a technical, data, or business field (or equivalent experience)

title: Site Reliability Engineer - Senior
description:
Overview:

SOFTSWISS is looking for an experienced Site Reliability Engineer to join our Sportsbook team and work on a high-load, production-critical platform.

About Product:

SOFTSWISS Sportsbook

Sportsbook is a software platform designed for launching and managing a successful online sports betting business. The Sportsbook team’s goal is to develop truly innovative software that will make the process of creating and running a bookmaker website faster and easier for our clients. We are searching for driven individuals who are passionate about what they do and are ready to work on engaging tasks and exciting projects together.

Purpose of the role:

You will work on a high-load platform in a production-focused role that combines backend engineering and operational responsibility. The work is hands-on: debugging real issues, stabilizing systems and improving reliability rather than building features in isolation.

Key responsibilities:

  • Investigate and resolve production issues across multiple services and integrations

  • Perform deep debugging (logs, traces, metrics, DB queries) to identify root causes

  • Tune system performance (PostgreSQL queries, caching, service behavior under load)

  • Work directly with Kubernetes environments: deployments, configs, scaling, troubleshooting

  • Improve observability: metrics, logging, tracing (Grafana, ELK stack)

  • Support and maintain integrations between Sportsbook services and external client platforms

  • Set up and configure new projects/environments (mainly Sportsbook-related)

  • Write internal tooling and automation in Go to reduce manual work and operational overhead

  • Work with messaging systems (Kafka, RabbitMQ) and diagnose related issues

  • Collaborate with developers, QA, and DevOps to resolve incidents and improve system stability

Required Experience:

  • Solid experience with Go (comfortable reading and writing production code)

  • Strong debugging skills: ability to trace issues across services, logs, and data layers

  • Experience working with PostgreSQL (query analysis, indexing, performance tuning)

  • Hands-on experience with Kubernetes (kubectl, deployments, configs, troubleshooting)

  • Familiarity with observability tools (Grafana, Kibana/ELK, logs/metrics/tracing)

  • Experience with Redis (caching patterns, debugging)

  • Experience with Kafka and/or RabbitMQ (consumer behavior, lag, retries, failures)

  • Understanding of how distributed systems behave under load (timeouts, retries, race conditions)

  • Comfortable working with production systems and handling incidents

  • Ability to work independently: take an issue, investigate, and drive it to resolution

Nice to have:

  • Experience with high-load or real-time systems

  • Experience with Sportsbook or betting platforms

  • Experience building internal tools or automation for engineering teams

Our Benefits:

  • Private health insurance

  • Sports benefits

  • Comprehensive Mental Health Program

  • Free English lessons (online)

  • Local language courses

  • Paid time off

  • Maternity leave support

  • Referral program rewards

  • Upskilling, internal workshops, and participation in professional conferences and corporate events

  • Develop, implement, and maintain manufacturing processes and procedures to ensure optimal production efficiency and product quality

  • Ensure compliance with safety regulations and quality standards in all manufacturing processes
  • Participate in equipment selection, installation, and qualification processes
  • Troubleshoot and resolve complex manufacturing equipment and process issues

The expected annual salary range for this role is $75,000 - $114,000 a year depending on experience. This position is also eligible for a variable incentive program.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE ROLE

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, preferably in Manufacturing, Electrical, Mechanical, or Industrial Engineering
  • Exposure to a manufacturing environment
  • Knowledge of automation equipment, including scanners, vision systems, and automated placement equipment
  • Proficiency in CAD software, preferably SolidWorks
  • Ability to read schematics and/or engineering drawings.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and experience with root cause analysis techniques
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite and manufacturing-related software applications

  • Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and lead cross-functional projects

Physical Requirements and Work Environment:

  • Must wear company-provided ESD safety-toed shoes, smock, and other PPE in required areas
  • Sitting or standing for 8+ hours, reaching, and using hands/fingers to operate a computer and other office equipment
  • Must be able to push, pull, reach, twist, turn, stoop for duration of 8+ hour shifts
  • Ability to lift or carry objects up to 40 lbs. unassisted
  • Ability to climb ladders
  • Ability to bend at waist and perform repetitive foot and hand action
  • Dexterity of hands and fingers to operate any required computer keyboard, mouse, and other technical instruments.

ADDITIONAL WAYS TO STAND OUT

  • 2+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering or a related field
  • Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes, automation technologies, PLC programming and continuous improvement methodologies
  • Demonstrated ability in electrical and pneumatic troubleshooting
  • Experience with a wide range of hand tools and mechanical assembly.

title: Web Engineer
description:

Our teams embrace modern engineering practices and are committed to delivering secure, scalable, and customer-focused solutions.
